assessment.nobel_worthiness: A foundational and unusually consequential body of political-economy research connecting political institutions, state capacity, electoral incentives and fiscal policy.
assessment.attribution: The listed scholars are central, complementary contributors to the modern analytical framework, though its broader intellectual lineage is extensive.
assessment.maturity: Theoretical contributions and empirical applications have accumulated over decades and substantially shaped research on institutions and development.
uncertainties: The contribution spans several linked literatures rather than a single sharply bounded discovery.
Credit allocation within political economy is inherently broad.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative-data research transformed measurement of intergenerational mobility and made place-based differences economically and policy relevant.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren and Friedman are highly identifiable leaders of the central empirical program.
assessment.maturity: The work has generated a durable research infrastructure, replications and a large subsequent literature.
uncertainties: The appropriate extent of credit to the wider administrative-data and mobility literature remains uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their reconstruction of long-run income and wealth distributions has fundamentally changed empirical research and public understanding of inequality.
assessment.attribution: The listed researchers have distinct and strongly documented roles in top-income measurement, long-run historical evidence and offshore wealth.
assessment.maturity: The data-building and measurement agenda has endured and supports an extensive international literature.
uncertainties: Tax-data coverage, wealth capitalization and offshore-asset measurement involve important assumptions.
The contribution joins multiple empirical projects with partially distinct claims.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This research gave rigorous empirical content to how technology, tasks and trade shocks reshape local labour markets and wage inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson are central to the influential task and China-shock research programs.
assessment.maturity: Its methods and findings have been scrutinized, extended and remain central to labour-market analysis.
uncertainties: Quantitative estimates and mechanisms vary across settings and empirical designs.
The candidate combines related but distinct technology and trade literatures.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The research established management practices and organizational capital as measurable, economically meaningful determinants of firm productivity.
assessment.attribution: Bloom and Van Reenen initiated the central measurement program, with Sadun a major contributor to its extension and interpretation.
assessment.maturity: Cross-country measurement, experiments and follow-on work give the program substantial empirical depth.
uncertainties: Separating causal effects of management from selection and correlated firm capabilities remains difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collateral constraints and financial-accelerator mechanisms supplied a durable framework for understanding amplification of macroeconomic fluctuations through credit markets.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore provided the seminal collateral framework, while Gertler made essential contributions to financial amplification in macroeconomics.
assessment.maturity: The mechanisms are embedded in modern macroeconomic modeling and gained renewed importance after financial crises.
uncertainties: Several related models and contributors complicate a clean three-person attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification redirected econometric practice toward credible conclusions when point identification depends on implausibly strong assumptions.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the defining intellectual originator, with Tamer and Molinari major contributors to moment-inequality methods and inference.
assessment.maturity: The framework is theoretically mature and broadly used across applied and structural econometrics.
uncertainties: The candidate packages a wide methodological literature whose boundaries are not uniquely defined.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM methods became core tools for empirical economics by addressing persistent outcomes, fixed effects and endogeneity in panel data.
assessment.attribution: Arellano, Blundell and Bond are directly associated with the canonical estimators and their practical development.
assessment.maturity: The methods are long established, widely implemented and supported by extensive theoretical and applied evaluation.
uncertainties: Finite-sample weakness, instrument proliferation and specification sensitivity limit reliability in some applications.
